bullets.title: Mag 7 All Higher Premarket; Broad Risk-On Setup
bullets.body: All Magnificent 7 stocks were trading higher premarket: Alphabet +1.3%, Meta +1%, Amazon +1%, Tesla +0.7%, Nvidia +0.6%, Microsoft +0.6%, Apple +0.4%. Cramer and others flagged a favorable setup across oil, bonds, and futures simultaneously.

bullets.title: US-Iran MOU: Hormuz Reopens in 30 Days, Markets Spike
bullets.body: A US-Iran memorandum of understanding stipulates reopening the Strait of Hormuz within 30 days and US withdrawal of forces from surrounding Iran — markets spiked on the headline. Brent crude dropped over 5% and S&P 500 futures extended gains to 0.7%. Iran's IRNA clarified it makes no commitment on transferring Hormuz management, and the nuclear file remains unresolved with talks to resume within 60 days.

bullets.title: Iran Deal Risk: Optimism Already Priced In, Upside Limited
bullets.body: One account warned that stocks, bonds, oil, and prediction markets are all converging on 'near certainty' the Iran conflict is over — meaning the risk is asymmetric to the downside if resolution is slower or messier than expected. Iran's state media simultaneously denied Hormuz status will be restored to pre-war levels, and no nuclear commitment was made.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO: Gray-Market Signals 35% Pop, 62% Odds of 20%+ Gain
bullets.body: SpaceX began trading on Nasdaq at 10 AM ET (ticker SPCX) with gray-market pricing signaling a ~35% opening pop. Prediction market odds of a 20%+ first-day gain surged to 62% from 20% the prior day; odds of a 30%+ gain stood at 46%, implying a $2.4T+ market cap. IPO valuation priced at $1.75T; Starlink reported $11.4B revenue and $4.4B operating profit in 2025 with subscribers growing from 2.3M in 2023 to 10M+ by early 2026.

bullets.title: Nasdaq-100 Rebalancing: NBIS, CRWV, ALAB Added; CHTR Removed
bullets.body: The Nasdaq-100 is rebalancing with Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Astera Labs (ALAB) being added to the index while Charter Communications (CHTR) is removed among others. Index inclusion flows typically drive forced buying in the added names.

bullets.title: Citi Upgrades AMD to Buy, Raises PT to $575 from $460
bullets.body: Citi upgraded AMD from Hold to Buy and raised its price target to $575 from $460, representing a 25% increase in the target.

bullets.title: AMZN: Record Operating Margins, Multiple AI/Growth Engines 'Setting Up'
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts flagged Amazon as a high-conviction long, citing record operating margins and growth vectors across AWS, advertising, Prime, healthcare, and AI — 'still early in AI, international e-commerce, and new verticals.' One account noted AMZN benefits both as an infrastructure enabler (AWS, chip supply) and as a retail operator as companies automate.

bullets.title: NVDA: China CPU Pivot + 6-Year Sharon AI Compute Deal
bullets.body: NVIDIA is pivoting to CPU products (Vera CPUs) for China sales after GPU export restrictions limited revenue, with multiple customers reportedly showing interest. Separately, Sharon AI announced a 6-year strategic compute collaboration with Nvidia, signaling extended data center pipeline demand.

bullets.title: Oracle EPS Beat but Analyst Issues Sell on Overvaluation
bullets.body: Oracle reported Q4 EPS of $2.03 vs. Wall Street consensus of $1.96, a clean beat. However, at least one analyst maintained a sell rating, arguing the stock has 'gotten ahead of itself' on valuation.

bullets.title: TSLA: GLJ Maintains Sell at $24.86, Calls Q2 Delivery Rebound Illusory
bullets.body: GLJ Research's Gordon Johnson kept Tesla on Sell Alert with a $24.86 price target, arguing that expected Q2 delivery improvements reflect inventory clearing and seasonal demand rather than renewed underlying strength.

bullets.title: Dan Ives: AI Dynamics Shifting — PLTR, SNOW, CRM Positioned to Thrive
bullets.body: Dan Ives flagged that AI market dynamics are changing and identified Palantir, Snowflake, and Salesforce as key beneficiaries. Palantir CEO Alex Karp separately expressed bullishness on the space sector and Elon's initiatives.

bullets.title: Japan Semiconductor Gas Supply Collapses on China Tungsten Embargo
bullets.body: China's export controls on tungsten caused Japan's semiconductor gas production to fall to zero, putting TSMC, SK Hynix, and Samsung supply chains at risk. A separate account noted China's WF6 export controls also disrupted Japan's supply chain affecting the same chip producers as part of broader AI supremacy competition and supply chain weaponization.

bullets.title: SOXL Drove $12B Rebalancing Demand = 45% of Prior-Day AUM
bullets.body: One account flagged that SOXL alone generated roughly $12B in net rebalancing demand, equal to approximately 45% of its prior-day AUM — highlighting how leveraged ETFs have become a 'dominant feature in current market structure.'

bullets.title: Macro: Inflation and Bond Yield Cycle Highs Are In; Short Oil Maintained
bullets.body: One macro account called cycle highs in both inflation and bond yields, maintaining short oil exposure with a disinflation thesis 'firmly intact.' They exited commodity and oil longs entered in February, though retained copper as one remaining inflation exposure (copper +2.3% on the session).

bullets.title: SPY Quad 1 Greenlight Signal; Financials Near 17th Percentile Positioning
bullets.body: SPY flashed a 'Quad 1 greenlight' technical signal suggesting positive momentum. Deutsche Bank positioning data shows Financials near the 17th historical percentile, meaning investors are significantly underweight the sector.

bullets.title: China Credit Data Beats: Aggregate Financing CNY17.48T vs CNY17.15T Est
bullets.body: China's May aggregate financing came in at CNY17.48T vs. the CNY17.15T estimate; new yuan loans hit CNY9.11T vs. CNY9.04T estimate; M1 accelerated to 5.5% vs. 5.0% expected. The credit beat suggests continued policy stimulus transmission into the real economy.

bullets.title: ChatGPT Hits 1 Billion Monthly Users Despite Souring AI Sentiment
bullets.body: ChatGPT has reached 1 billion monthly app users, per a CNBC report flagged on fintwit, even as one account argued that once AI models reach sufficient capability thresholds, consumers will shift to cost optimization and open-source alternatives will gain share.

bullets.title: Record ~$8T in Money Market Cash Supporting Tech Buildout
bullets.body: One account flagged that money market cash is near a record $8 trillion, which it sees as fuel for major capital-raising exercises and the current technological buildout — citing the historic SpaceX IPO as emblematic of this dynamic.

bullets.title: Intel-TSMC: Intel Fellow Reportedly Considered Suing TSMC Over CoWoS-L IP
bullets.body: An Intel Fellow reportedly once considered suing TSMC, alleging TSMC's CoWoS-L silicon bridge technology copied Intel's silicon bridge concept. No litigation was filed per the report, but the anecdote highlights ongoing IP tension between the two.

bullets.title: Industrials +15% Since October vs Mag 7 -5%; SpaceX Named as Driver
bullets.body: One account noted that since October, industrials are up 15% while the Mag 7 is down 5% — with SpaceX cited as a key performance driver behind the rotation. The observation frames the SpaceX IPO as a macro rotation catalyst rather than just an isolated event.
